text:
marc: Heads up — getting a bunch of 429s from EU GPU pool this morning, but SDKs aren't getting any hint headers. client teams seeing exponential retries.

anna: Ops alert fired at 09:12. Pool fill at 98% and pending queue spiking.

ops-bot: [incident] gpu-pool-eu-high-fill created. autoscaler paused due to quota. https://infra.redwood/incident/4532

marc: We currently return 429 only with occasional Retry-After. That's too coarse; clients need an admission/cooldown signal + estimated window so they can reduce concurrency instead of hammering.

toshi: Agreed. Proposal: add header `X-RW-ADMIT` with a tiny semi-colon delimited payload: `status=defer;wait_ms=1200;pool_pct=6` — simple parse, human readable, no JSON to avoid header size bloat.

sam: I like a short name but prefer `X-RW-ADMIT` over `X-RW-Cooldown`. Also want explicit statuses: `reject` (immediate drop), `defer` (try later), `accept-queued`.

anna: Need to decide semantics around `wait_ms=0` — is that accepted but queued, or immediate suggested retry? We should be explicit.

marc: Draft semantics: when returning 429, header must include `status` and `wait_ms`. Interpretations: `reject` = drop request (client should fail fast), `defer` = backoff for wait_ms then retry, `accept-queued` = request queued server-side and client may poll or open streaming connection. If header absent, fallback to Retry-After or exponential backoff.

kai: Minimal SDK change: if resp.status == 429 then parse `X-RW-ADMIT`; if present, use jittered backoff around wait_ms (e.g., uniform[wait_ms*0.5, wait_ms*1.5]). If absent, fallback to Retry-After or base 1s exp backoff. Example: 
```
if (resp.status == 429) {
  const admit = resp.headers['x-rw-admit'];
  if (admit) { /* parse status, wait_ms */ jitteredWait(parseInt(wait_ms)); }
  else { exponentialBackoff(); }
}
```

marc: Also suggest optional `pool_pct` to let clients know how full the pool is (helps aggressive vs conservative clients). Not required.

toshi: Implementation notes: runtime emits header at admission point. Edge proxy will proxy the header through. Feature-flag it for EU region first. We'll need to ensure header is added only on 429 and not on every response to keep header churn low.

sam: SDK impact: small, one-line header check, single new behavior flag. We'll ship behind minor semver bump. I can open PR for JS/Go clients after we lock header format.

anna: Ops concerns: adding header is negligible cost, but happy-path code must not regress. Also add metric for `admit.header_present` to measure adoption.

ops-bot: autoscaler action: if fill>95% and pending>200 then spawn +2 nodes (cooldown 10m). Logged.

marc: Cost note — better backoff reduces wasted GPU time and lowers cost; header may slightly increase request header size but should pay off.

kai: Suggest we publish a short doc snippet (SDKs should treat header as advisory, not authoritative; fallbacks required). Also show sample parsing code and recommended jitter formula.

devx: I'll add a quickstart update and sample to /docs/sdk/backpressure.md once header is final. Also will add note to changelog for client teams.

marc: Plan: get header RFC in PR today, runtime change feature-flagged Wed, enable EU Thu morning, monitor 24h; rollback if error rate doesn't drop. Anyone object?

sam: No objections. I'll draft SDK PRs after RFC.

toshi: I'll take runtime patch. Will coordinate with edge team for header pass-through.

anna: I'll monitor metrics and post a short summary in #incidents after rollout.

marc: Great. Follow-ups in #eng-runtime if anything breaks :thumbsup:
